coverageVocabulary.exact-executable-regression: a green test that fails on the real defect and is reachable from the canonical gate
coverageVocabulary.unit-level-semantics: the semantic unit is asserted in isolation (classification, encoding domain, effect registry) without a compiled program
coverageVocabulary.synthetic-only: the artefact under test is constructed inside the test rather than produced by a real toolchain
coverageVocabulary.partial: some real evidence exists but a stated part of the dimension is unproven
coverageVocabulary.unknown: cannot be determined from the repository without executing an unavailable toolchain or artefact

gaps.dimension: ARM64 real-machine-byte decompiler route (decoded instruction -> shared semantic pipeline)
currentEvidence: tools/validation/phase8/build-corpus.mjs:31-37 declares arm64 as representation 'assembly' while x86_64/riscv64 are 'machine-bytes'
tests/phase8/corpus/functions.json: arm64 entries carry an 'assembly' string, x86_64/riscv64 entries carry frozen linked bytes
js/targets/architecture/arm64/ contains only encoding-word.js, memory-access-qualifiers.js and effects/ — there is no decoded-instruction provider and no semantic-function entry
tests/phase8/corpus/explicit-compiler-abi.test.mjs:49 and tests/phase8/provenance/navigation.test.mjs:24 iterate only ['x86_64','riscv64']
gaps.missingEvidence: A test that loads a real ARM64 object/executable, decodes it with the shipped Capstone artifact, enters the shared Semantic IR/CFG/SSA/MemorySSA pipeline, and asserts recovered semantics for the same source as the other two architectures.
gaps.productRisk: Highest in this audit. ARM64 is the primary product target (iOS/iPad-first). Its decompiler input is assembler text re-parsed test-side, which can differ from real Capstone operand text, and its instruction stream never passes through the shipped decoder in the quality corpus. A decoder-text or loader-layer defect is therefore invisible to the strongest existing decompiler gate.
gaps.benchmarkOverfitRisk: low — asserting this does not resemble any CodeFuse scoring surface
gaps.recommendedFixtureStyle: Owned source -> real clang/lld AArch64 ELF, sha256-pinned, reusing the provenance shape already proven in tests/scpa/fixtures/*.json (source sha, binary sha, rebuild command, expectedFunctions, explicit claim string). Assert semantic equivalence with an independently evaluated source-level oracle, not with a printed-text snapshot.
gaps.approximateExecutionCost: estimated 1-3 s per case after build; fixture build cost is a one-time pinned artefact with a recorded rebuild command

tests/scpa/swift-generic.test.mjs and tests/issue-*-swift-* assert Swift metadata/witness structures, not decompiled semantics
gaps.missingEvidence: Any executed Swift ARM64 case: real swiftc output, real binary, asserted semantics or even asserted non-regression.
gaps.productRisk: High. Swift is the dominant iOS language; the entire Swift decompiler path is unproven end-to-end and can regress without any gate turning red.
gaps.benchmarkOverfitRisk: low — CodeFuse's frozen ARM64 set is C/C++ only
gaps.recommendedFixtureStyle: Same owned compiler-twin shape as G-01 but with a pinned swiftc version, and a hard fail-closed prerequisite when swiftc is absent (BLOCKING, never skipped).
gaps.approximateExecutionCost: estimated 20-60 s for the whole Swift lane (toolchain startup dominates); pathological cases separated into a higher tier

currentEvidence: tests/competitive-arm64 recipes 'rust-micro' and 'go-micro' exist with pinned compiler argv but no runner executes them

tests/issue-3715-rust-v0-impl-disambiguator.mjs, tests/issue-6182/6203/6237/6239-rust-*.mjs, tests/issue-5347-go-rtype-nameoff.test.mjs, tests/issue-7879-go-runtime-types-completeness.mjs assert symbol/metadata decoding only
gaps.missingEvidence: Decompiler semantics or even loader-to-analysis acceptance for rustc/go-produced ARM64 binaries.
gaps.productRisk: Medium-high. Rust and Go binaries are common analysis targets and their symbol/ABI conventions differ enough that metadata-only coverage does not bound decompiler behaviour.
gaps.recommendedFixtureStyle: Reuse the existing 6-recipe manifest identity rather than a parallel format: extend tools/competitive-arm64 with an executable owned-fixture lane, or add a compiler-truth language lane with fail-closed toolchain prerequisites.
gaps.approximateExecutionCost: estimated 20-60 s per language lane; rustc/go startup dominates, deferred tier acceptable

currentEvidence: 42 of tests/phase4/binary reference arm64 but fixtures are built in-test with DataView writers (e.g. tests/phase4/binary/issue-3615-macho-arm64-32-indirect-pointer-width.test.mjs:25-71); only 1 of 197 files reads a checked-in binary
tests/fixtures/real-binaries.json pins three large iOS images that are absent from the tree (tests/battlecats|TsumTsum|YWP contain 62-69 byte placeholders)
npm run accuracy is not part of npm run check
gaps.missingEvidence: A small, in-repo, sha256-pinned real Mach-O ARM64 binary (or a compiler-produced one) taken through open -> analyze -> decompile in the canonical gate.
gaps.productRisk: High. Mach-O is the shipping platform container; Mach-O parsing/section/discovery defects are only exercised against hand-built bytes whose shape is written by the same authors who wrote the parser.
gaps.recommendedFixtureStyle: Compiler-produced Mach-O ARM64 is hard without an Apple SDK; prefer a minimal owned Mach-O ARM64 fixture whose bytes are produced by a pinned local assembler/linker recipe and whose digest is frozen, plus an explicit statement that it is not Apple-toolchain evidence. Keep the large real images as a separate opt-in tier.
gaps.approximateExecutionCost: estimated <1 s per fixture once built

currentEvidence: tests/phase4/binary/issue-3673-pe-arm64-reloc-whitelist.test.mjs, issue-4162-pe-arm64-xdata-handler-rva.test.mjs, tests/pe-arm64-xdata-*.test.mjs, tests/issue-8474-pe-arm64-xdata-unwind-codes.test.mjs cover container and unwind decoding
gaps.missingEvidence: A real PE32+ ARM64 binary reaching the analysis/decompile path.
gaps.productRisk: Medium. PE/ARM64 (Windows-on-ARM) is secondary but its parser is large; synthetic-only coverage means the byte-builder and the parser can share one blind spot.
gaps.recommendedFixtureStyle: One owned, digest-pinned PE32+ ARM64 fixture produced by a recorded recipe, asserted through the loader and the unwind path only (not decompiler semantics).

currentEvidence: tests/machine-effects/arm64-a64-fp-denominator.test.mjs and arm64-a64-simd-denominator.test.mjs assert registry ownership over enumerated encodings
tests/machine-effects/arm64-fp-*.test.mjs, arm64-simd-*.test.mjs, issue-4201-arm64-fp-advsimd-access-traps.test.mjs assert operand/modifier domains
tests/phase8/foundation/issue-5454-movi2d-immediate.test.mjs and issue-6207-fcsel-fccmp-condition-domain.mjs assert individual lowering contracts
gaps.missingEvidence: Any compiler-produced ARM64 function whose floating-point or SIMD semantics are asserted after decompilation (vector code from -O2/-O3 loops, HFA arguments, lane operations).
gaps.productRisk: High. FP/SIMD is where a decoder-owned notion of correctness most easily diverges from recovered source semantics, and the frozen corpus has no such case in either lane.
gaps.benchmarkOverfitRisk: medium — CodeFuse's frozen set is scalar C and its reference is IDA output; FP cases must be designed from the source language, not from any reference text
gaps.recommendedFixtureStyle: Source-level functions with a declared mathematical contract (e.g. a dot product, a clamp, an fma chain) with an independently computed expected result over a value set, exactly like tests/compiler-truth's boundary evaluation.

currentEvidence: tests/machine-effects/arm64-atomic-*.test.mjs, issue-8603-arm64-atomic-zr-acquire.test.mjs, issue-8607-arm64-ldar-zr-acquire.test.mjs assert effect classification

tests/machine-effects/fixtures/formal-source/aarch64-{relaxed,acquire,release,acq-rel,seq-cst}.litmus plus tools/validation/machine-effects/oracle-evidence-v2.mjs assert claim-local permitted/forbidden outcome sets
gaps.missingEvidence: A compiled ARM64 function containing an explicit atomic sequence whose recovered semantics are asserted (or whose unknown status is asserted to remain explicit).
gaps.productRisk: Medium-high. Ordering bugs are the classic silent-wrong-answer class in an analyzer; the formal evidence is deliberately claim-local and cannot bound the lifter.
gaps.recommendedFixtureStyle: Owned source using an explicit atomic builtin sequence, with two oracles: an exact semantic assertion where the product claims exactness, and an explicit 'unknown preserved' assertion where it does not. Never accept a silent drop to raw assembly.

gaps.dimension: ABI argument passing, returns, aggregates, varargs — validated at a real call site
currentEvidence: ~60 files across tests/phase6/abi, tests/phase8/abi, tests/semantic-v2/aapcs64-argument-classification.test.mjs assert classification and placement rules as units
tests/semantic-v2/aapcs64-argument-classification.test.mjs and tests/phase8/abi/c3-combined-acceptance.test.mjs validate the required profile matrix
no test in this set compiles a function that actually passes an HFA by value or returns a 17-byte struct
gaps.missingEvidence: A function pair (caller + callee) compiled for ARM64 where the argument/return classification is observable in the recovered code or in the analysis result, with an independently computed expectation.
gaps.productRisk: High. A classification that is right in isolation can still be attached to the wrong physical registers or stack slots at a real call site, which is exactly the failure a user notices.
gaps.benchmarkOverfitRisk: low — CodeFuse does not exercise aggregates or varargs
gaps.recommendedFixtureStyle: Source-defined struct/HFA/vararg cases with an oracle derived from the source and the AAPCS64 rule text (not from another tool's output), asserted on the analysis result and on the recovered prototype/argument binding.

currentEvidence: tests/competitive-arm64 declares an allowlisted strip-only twin policy in tools/competitive-arm64/manifest.mjs policies.twins, but no twin has ever been built (binaryTwinsVerified: false)
the three tests/scpa ELF fixtures are unstripped and carry expectedFunctions from their own manifests
gaps.missingEvidence: Any executed test comparing the same ARM64 binary with and without debug/symbol information.
gaps.productRisk: Medium-high. Real analysis targets are usually stripped; a suite that only ever sees debug info silently assumes symbol authority that production does not have.
gaps.benchmarkOverfitRisk: medium — CodeFuse's own family is 'with vs without -g'; the new twins must be chosen for our invariants (same-or-better explicit unknown), not to mirror that grid
gaps.recommendedFixtureStyle: One linked debug artefact copied and then strip-allowlisted (exactly the existing declared policy), asserted as a pair: neither twin may silently degrade a declared-exact result, and a symbol-dependent claim must become explicitly unknown rather than wrong.
gaps.approximateExecutionCost: estimated +1 strip step (<1 s) per twin at build time

gaps.dimension: Optimization sweep beyond -O0/-O1/-O2 inside the gate
currentEvidence: the frozen corpus covers -O0/-O1/-O2 only (tools/validation/phase8/build-corpus.mjs OPTIMIZATION_LEVELS)
-O3/-Os/-Oz exist only in tests/compiler-truth, which is not in the canonical gate
CodeFuse covers O0/O1/O2/O3/Os but only as an external scoreboard
gaps.productRisk: Medium. Aggressive optimization is the normal shipping configuration for iOS release builds and is where inlining/idiom folding tests the decompiler hardest.
gaps.benchmarkOverfitRisk: high if the new grid is copied from CodeFuse's exact {O0,O1,O2,O3,Os} x {g,no_g} shape; design the optimization set from the compiler behaviour under test and include at least one level CodeFuse does not use
gaps.recommendedFixtureStyle: Add -O3/-Os/-Oz to a new owned source-based lane; do not extend the frozen Phase 8 corpus in place, because that invalidates its frozen baseline (a deliberate documented transaction).

currentEvidence: tests/compiler-truth uses clang/clang++/swiftc only (tests/compiler-truth/run-core.mjs:107, language-matrix.mjs:17,168)
the frozen Phase 8 corpus records an Ubuntu clang 18.1.3 toolchain only
CodeFuse includes gcc-derived cases but only as external comparison material
gaps.missingEvidence: Any in-gate ARM64 case produced by a second compiler family.
gaps.productRisk: Medium-high. Independent-verifier discipline requires enumerated compiler families; a single available compiler must not silently satisfy a multi-family contract (docs/ENGINEERING_PROCESS_GUARDRAILS.md section 3.5).

gaps.recommendedFixtureStyle: A second compiler family must be a BLOCKING enumerated requirement with recorded version/target, not an optional extra; if the family is unavailable the suite must fail closed rather than skip.
gaps.approximateExecutionCost: estimated 1-3 s per case; requires a pinned aarch64-capable gcc

gaps.dimension: False-green resistance of the new coverage itself
currentEvidence: the A2 locked denominator already forbids claiming full ISA coverage and exposes blocking gaps explicitly (tests/machine-effects/a2-denominator.test.mjs:19-25)
the Phase 8 verifier already derives hard-zero counters from a frozen baseline and compares determinism across two runs (tools/validation/phase8/metrics.mjs:315-410, MEASUREMENT_TIME_BUDGET_MS)
the SCPA manifests already carry explicit non-claim strings and sha256 identity for both source and binary
the machine-effects prerequisites already fail closed on a missing pinned toolchain
gaps.missingEvidence: These disciplines are per-suite, not shared: no common excluded_by_environment counter, no common 'declared-precision vs achieved-precision' separation, and OBS-3 shows one suite where a missing language is a silent skip.
gaps.productRisk: High in aggregate. A new suite that reuses none of this would be able to report 100% while measuring nothing.
gaps.recommendedFixtureStyle: Mandate the existing patterns by reference: hard-zero counters, frozen-baseline comparison, two-run determinism, a fail-closed prerequisite assertion, and an explicit counted excluded-by-environment set that can never be quietly empty.
gaps.approximateExecutionCost: structural; the determinism double-run is the only visible cost and it should be confined to Tier 0

compiler-truth, out of gate, assembly text; Darwin runtime unproven

crossCuttingConclusions: Decoder instruction coverage is not decompiler end-to-end recovery, and the repository is strong on the former and structurally weak on the latter for ARM64 specifically.
No existing ARM64 evidence connects a compiler-produced binary to a semantic equivalence oracle inside the canonical gate.

Three independent coverage-integrity conditions were observed at the base SHA (OBS-1..OBS-3): one red canonical-gate test on the ARM64 decompiler lane, one fail-closed missing toolchain, and one silently-skipped mandatory language.

The highest-overfit-risk surface is the CodeFuse-shaped grid (ARM64 C, clang/gcc, five optimization levels, with/without debug, IDA reference). Any new suite must differ from that grid in at least the source set, the oracle type, and the optimization set, and must never gate on similarity to a reference text.
